Add historical group membership from the NCCS group metadata

Source: R/md-ingest-group-meta.R
md_ingest_group_meta.Rd

metadata-group-number records, per EIN, the group exemption number observed across vintages as a ;;-delimited history, plus .last and .best resolutions of it.

Usage

md_ingest_group_meta(con = NULL, path = NULL, version = "2023-09")

Arguments

con

A connection from md_db().

path

Path to metadata-group-number.csv.

version

Pinned meta_group_number version.

Value

Row counts, invisibly.

This is a small source, and saying so is part of the job

Measured against the database before loading it:


                       meta file     BMF
  EINs with a GEN         33,274   647,569
  distinct GENs            2,958     4,917

Of the 33,274, 27,065 agree with the BMF, 5,180 carry a GEN the BMF does not, and 1,219 disagree. The net contribution is 2,913 new parent-to-member pairs against 320,117 already present - under 1%.

It is loaded anyway because those 5,180 are not noise: an EIN whose history records a group the current BMF does not is one that left a group, and former membership is exactly what explains a lingering name similarity to a national parent. That is worth having in a disambiguation database even at this volume. What would not be worth having is pretending it is bigger.

Conflicts resolve to the BMF, on vintage rather than preference

The 1,219 disagreements are settled by taking the BMF's value, because this file is a 2023-09 extract and the pinned BMF is 2026-07. That is a statement about which snapshot is more recent, not a judgement that NCCS is less reliable than the IRS. If a newer group extract arrives the rule should be re-examined rather than inherited.

In practice the rule is enforced by construction: rows are only added for EINs where the BMF has no GEN at all, so a conflict can never overwrite anything. The count is reported so the disagreement is visible rather than absorbed.

Why the other two files are not loaded

metadata-group-aff and metadata-group-return are the same 835,340 EINs with group.aff.incl and group.return flags, and both are 95.4% null. What they describe is filing behaviour - whether an organisation is included in a group return - rather than structure. That is a property of a filing, not a relation between two EINs, so it has no home in ein_relation and no bearing on disambiguation. They stay registered and unloaded.
